#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Introduces an option to enable concurrent mode in the kubectl delete command, improving performance by allowing resources to be deleted in parallel.
#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--

-->
Fixes #125407

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
This is a work in progress—please confirm if the implementation is on the right track.
I have conducted initial tests using my EKS cluster:

Test with 10 deployments:
Concurrent: 3.713 seconds
Non-concurrent: 5.509 seconds

Test with 20 deployments:
Concurrent: 5.878 seconds
Non-concurrent: 9.192 seconds

Test with 35 deployments:
Concurrent: 8.802 seconds
Non-concurrent: 14.727 seconds

issue_context.title: kubectl delete a large number of objects taking too long
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Make `kubectl delete` execute more efficiently. There are two options to make it happen:

1. implement `deletecollection` in kubectl instead of one-by-one deletions
2. Make one-by-one deletions concurrent

Some history digging found `deletioncollection` was not preferable to some extent https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/90743

### Why is this needed?

kubectl delete a large number of objects taking too long. For example, deleting about 650 events takes 3m49.077s whereas using `deletecollection` only takes 6s
comments: From the options given I think implementing deletecollection in kubectl is the most simple and straighforward solution. Deleting them concurrently might introduce more complexity, race conditions, etc. One downside of deletecollection is that it might block other changes to the resources that might have to wait for deletecollection to finish.

Actually implementing concurrent deletion might be more straightforward in current kubectl code as it just queries the object list and iterates them for deleting. The deleting is supposed to be independent as the object key is provided to call delete API so race conditions can be avoided as well.
